questions.question_text: A marked price is 50% above cost. A retailer subtracts Rs 360 from the mark and then gives 5% off the reduced price. If cost is Rs 2,400, what is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Marked price=Rs 3,600; after the fixed reduction and 5% discount, SP=3,240x0.95=Rs 3,078. Gain=678/2,400=28.25%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A seller gains 20% after allowing a 10% discount on the marked price. By what percent is the marked price above cost?
questions.explanation: 0.9 MP=1.2 CP, so MP/CP=4/3: 33 1/3% above cost.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A marked price of Rs 5,000 is reduced by successive discounts of 10% and 12.5%, then a Rs 300 coupon is applied. What is the effective discount percentage?
questions.explanation: The successive discounts leave Rs 5,000x0.9x0.875=Rs 3,937.50. After the coupon, Rs 3,637.50 is paid; the discount is 1,362.50/5,000=27.25%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: An article's marked price is Rs 4,800. A discount of 15% is followed by a second discount of x%, giving a selling price of Rs 3,468. Find x.
questions.explanation: After first discount price=4,080; second reduction=612, or 15%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper marks an item 25% above cost and then gives two equal successive discounts totaling 36% of the marked price. What is each discount rate?
questions.explanation: For equal rate r, 1-(1-r)^2=.36, so 1-r=.8, r=20%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper sells goods at a 10% discount on marked price and uses a 900 g weight for each kilogram. The marked price is 25% above the cost per true kilogram. What is his profit percentage on actual goods supplied?
questions.explanation: For each 0.9 kg delivered, revenue is 0.9x1.25=1.125 times the cost per kg. The goods cost 0.9 times the cost per kg, so the gain rate is (1.125-0.9)/0.9=25%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A retailer marks goods 80% above cost, gives a discount of 25%, and then charges 5% tax on the discounted bill. Treating the tax as collected for the government, what is the retailer's profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Net retailer receipt before tax=1.8 x .75=1.35 CP, hence 35% gain.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A dishonest dealer claims to sell at cost price but gives only 750 g instead of 1 kg. He also grants a 10% discount on the quoted price. What is his net profit percentage if the quoted price equals cost per kilogram?
questions.explanation: Revenue=.9 CP for goods costing .75 CP; gain=.15/.75=20%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A shop offers successive discounts of 30% and 20%. A third discount of x% makes the total equivalent discount exactly 60%. Find x.
questions.explanation: After the first two discounts, 0.7x0.8=0.56 of MP remains. For the final price to be 0.40 MP, the last factor is 0.40/0.56=5/7, so the third discount is 2/7=28 4/7%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper buys an article for Rs 1,800, marks it 50% above cost, gives a 20% discount, then grants a Rs 180 coupon. A salesperson receives 5% commission on the amount paid. What is the shopkeeper's net profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Marked price=Rs 2,700; after 20% off and the Rs 180 coupon, collection=Rs 1,980. Commission=Rs 99, leaving Rs 1,881 against cost Rs 1,800; net gain=81/1,800 x 100=4.5%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A dealer buys an item at 25% below its marked price and sells it at a 10% discount on the marked price. What is his profit percentage on his purchase price?
questions.explanation: Let MP=100; CP=75, SP=90; profit rate=15/75=20%.

questions.question_text: A retailer sells an item at a 15% profit after allowing a 25% discount. If the cost price is Rs 2,400 and the marked price is rounded up to the next Rs 100, what is the actual profit percentage if he gives the stated discount on that rounded mark?
questions.explanation: Required unrounded MP=2,760/.75=3,680, rounded up=3,700; SP=2,775; gain=375/2,400=15.625%.

questions.question_text: A shop's marked price on an item is Rs 5,000. Its discount is reduced from 20% to 12%. By what percentage does the amount collected increase?
questions.explanation: The collected price rises from Rs 4,000 to Rs 4,400, an increase of Rs 400/4,000=10%.

questions.question_text: An item is marked at Rs 6,000. Offer A gives 30% off; Offer B gives successive discounts of 20% and 8%. Which offer gives the lower price, and by how much?
questions.explanation: Offer A price=6,000x0.70=Rs 4,200. Offer B price=6,000x0.80x0.92=Rs 4,416. Offer A is lower by Rs 216.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper marks goods 50% above cost, then gives successive discounts of 10% and 10%. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Selling-price factor=1.50x0.90x0.90=1.215 of cost, giving a 21.5% profit.

questions.question_text: A retailer marks an item 40% above cost. After giving a 10% discount, he earns Rs 260. What is the cost price?
questions.explanation: Selling price is 1.40x0.90=1.26 times cost. A Rs 260 profit is 26% of cost, so cost=Rs 1,000.

questions.question_text: A trader marks goods 60% above cost and gives a 25% discount. He also bears a delivery expense equal to 3% of cost. Find his net profit percentage.
questions.explanation: Sales revenue=1.6x.75=1.2C; net after .03C delivery expense =1.17C, so 17%.
questions.source: Original SSC-style practice question; adapted from reviewed Profit & Loss bank

questions.question_text: A retailer buys an article at a 15% discount on its marked price and later sells it at a 10% discount on that same mark. What profit percentage does he earn on his purchase cost?
questions.explanation: Let MP=100. CP=85 and SP=90, so profit rate=5/85 x 100=5 15/17%.

questions.question_text: On a Rs 50,000 bill, compare a single 20% discount with successive discounts of 16% and 4%. What is the difference in the amounts discounted?

questions.question_text: A notebook costs a shopkeeper Rs 85. After allowing a 15% discount, the shopkeeper earns 20% on cost. What was its marked price?

questions.question_text: A trader gives an 18% discount on the marked price and earns 6.6% on cost. By what percentage is the mark above cost?

questions.question_text: For the larger of these offers, buy 3 and get 4 free or buy 5 and get 6 free, what is its equivalent discount rate?
questions.explanation: First offer: 4/7 = 57.14%; second: 6/11 = 54.55%; the first is larger.

questions.question_text: A bottle has an MRP of Rs 20. Under a buy 2, get 1 free offer, what is the effective discount percentage?
questions.explanation: Pay Rs 40 for goods listed at Rs 60; discount = 20/60 x 100 = 33.33%.

questions.question_text: A buyer gets 3 bananas free on buying 12 and then receives a further 25% bill discount. What is the equivalent discount?
questions.explanation: Free quantity gives 20% off; successive reduction = 1 - .80 x .75 = 40%.
